questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **incommunicable.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct spelling is** I-N-C-O-M-M-U-N-I-C-A-B-L-E. **
 
• It means **incapable of being communicated or shared. it is an adjective.**
 
 
• Ex. ‘*It is difficult to share the incommunicable experiences of war.’*
 
 
 
• **Communicate: Share or exchange information,** news, or ideas. 
 
• Communicable: Able to communicate.
 
• The English **prefix 'in' can also, however, mean “not.” **Some examples of 'in' meaning “not” include insane, or “not” sane, independent, or “not” dependent, and **in****c**ommunicable or **“not” **communicable.

 

Hence, the correct answer is ***'I**ncommunicable.'*

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

When we use our

A - beauty to group others, we

B - personal standards for

C - promote a kind of apartheid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is BAC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first sentence in the sequence should suitably follow ‘our’. A verb cannot follow so we cannot have sentence C as the first sentence in the sequence (‘our promote a kind…’ is not correct). Sentence B seems to be a proper sentence to follow ‘our’.
 
• ‘When we use our personal standards for…’
 
• Now, the **question arises – personal standards for what?**
 
• So, the **next sentence can be A – personal standards for beauty**.
 
• ‘When we use our personal standards for beauty to group others …’ - This is leading to a meaningful sentence.
 
• ​The sentence is completed when C becomes the final part.

 

**Correct sentence:__ ***‘When we use our personal standards for beauty to group others, we promote a kind of apartheid’*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Partition (has been billed) as a distressing phase in the subcontinent’s history.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **No improvement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word ***partition* is a singular noun**. So, ***has* and not *have* should follow**. So, we can eliminate option 1.
 
• Also, when the structure of the sentence is **‘*****has been + verb**’*, the **verb takes its past participle form.**
 
 
• Let us understand this by example:
 
 
• *The cars have been **washed**. (past participle form of wash)*
 
• *The car has been **manufactured** by the Tata Group. (past participle form of manufacture)*
 
 
 
 
 
• Hence, we can eliminate option 3. (*billed* should be used and not *bill*)
 
• ‘*Partition has been billed …*’ **is correct **and needs no improvement.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.
 
• Note – the word** *billed *here means to declare officially.**

 

**Correct sentence:**__** '***The Partition has been billed (declared) as a distressing phase in the subcontinent’s history.'*

**Correct sentence*:***__ '*I worry that social media (is killing) creativity.'*

• **Scant** – **Very little or not sufficient**, barely amounting to a specified number or quantity

• **Deluge** – **a very large amount of water** or rain, a severe flood.
 
 
• Ex.* A deluge of rain hit the plains*

• Ex. *A plethora of letters*
 
 
 
• **Surfeit **– **an excessive amount of something.**
 
 
• Ex. *A surfeit of blood*
 
 
 
• The word *scant *expresses the desired meaning.**
 

Hence, the correct answer is *'Scant'.***

questions.question: find this blind _____________ of illogical ideas
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Acceptance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Looking at the structure of the sentence, we need a noun in the blank.
 
• The preposition **'*of'* follows a noun** and not a verb.
 
• Note__ – The meaning of the word multitude: a large number of people 
 
• 
 **Acceptance (noun) -** **the action of consenting to receive** or undertake something offered or believe or **come to recognize as valid **or correct. ex. *charges involving the acceptance of bribes*
 
 
• **Accept (verb)** - **Consent to receive** or undertake (something offered). ex.* he accepted a pen as a present*
 
• **Acceptor** **(noun)** - a person or thing that accepts or receives something.
 
• **Acceptant (Adjective)** - willingly accepting (something).
 
• Here we have to use 'Acceptance' (come to recognize as valid), as acceptance of illogical idea makes sense. other options don't make sense. 

 

__**Correct sentence:**__ '*find this blind acceptance of illogical ideas by the multitude'.*

questions.question: solemnly and _____________. Particularly in the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Authoritatively**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Since the **conjunction *and* **is used before the blank, the **word that fills the blank should be similar to ‘solemnly’. **
 
• Also, the word should be equivalent in structure i.e., *and *connects two similar forms of words: Consider ‘…A and B…’ If A is a noun, so is B. If A is an adverb, so is B.
 
 
• For example, She likes cooking and dancing (not she likes cooking and to dance)
 
 
 
• Here, **‘solemnly’ is an adverb – a word that adds a description to the verb.** (**usually, adverbs end with –ly** )
 
• ***Solemnly* means showing determination and seriousness.**
 
• We need an adverb to fill the blank in a similar context. Option 1 seems appropriate.
 
• ***Authoritatively* means in a confident and respected manner.**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__ '*solemnly and Authoritatively Particularly in the**'*.

questions.question: ideas are accepted _________ dispute or examination,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Without.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• We need to understand the** tone and the context** of the sentence. The author states that the **most illogical ideas are accepted **(ideas which are not reasonable and lack logic).
 
• Now, we can sense the **author’s surprise, shock or concern in this sentence**.
 
• So, the **most appropriate** word to fill the blank will be ***without*.**
 
• This highlights the concerned tone of author. (If the most illogical ideas are debated or examined, then there will no hint of concerned tone in the sentence – so we cannot use ‘with’)

 

**Correct sentence:__** ‘*The most illogical ideas are accepted without dispute or examination…*’

questions.question: absurd ideas _________ truth, providing
questions.solution:
The correct answer is As.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘As’ **is used to mean to the** same extent or degree.** Here, the sentence conveys that people take absurd ideas equal to truth.
 
• **As** is a conjunction. A conjunction is a more simple connecting word— it can connect everything from full sentences to individual words and does not itself define the relationship between the two items it connects.
 
• **'Like'** is a preposition that means 'similar to'. A preposition is a word that positions nouns in relation to one another, i.e. the when, where, and how regarding the noun’s role in a sentence: in the house, at home, like him etc.
 
• **Such **- 
 of the type previously mentioned. Ex. "I have been involved in many such courses"
 
 
• 
 **Just** - very recently; in the immediate past. Ex.* I've just seen the local paper *
 
 
• 
 **'As' **fits perfectly in the given blank. 
 

Correct sentence:__ ‘*absurd ideas **as** truth, providing*’

The meaning conveyed by the sentence in both voices will remain the same. Only sequence of the subject and the object (or the action) changes.

In Active voice – Subject + verb + object is the sequence.

In Passive voice – Object + verb + Subject is the sequence.

When the

P : demonstrate that these are wholly inhuman

Q : state identifies some practices

R : as incompatible with the ‘civilised’ norms, it must
questions.solution:

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

During the later 19th and early 20th centuries, (1)/ forest preservation programmes were established (2)/ in British India, the United States, and Europe. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The error lies in part 1 of the sentence. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

Here, instead of *later, *we should use ***late***. ‘During the late 19th century’, ‘In the late 19th century', 'By the late 19th century' etc. are the correct ways in which we indicate the later part of the years 1801-1899.

__Correct sentence__ - During the **late** 19th and early 20th centuries, forest preservation programmes were established in British India, the United States, and Europe.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Playing sports and doing any form (1)/ of physical activity can trigger (2)/ the production of endorphins. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The sentence is grammatically correct and contains no error. Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

‘The’ is used before singular and plural nouns when the noun is specific. So, the use of ‘the’ before *production of endorphins *is correct. (‘… can trigger production of endorphins’ would have been incorrect).
